Definition: properly, feminine of Ludios (of foreign origin) (a Lydian, in Asia Minor); Lydia, a Christian woman:--Lydia.
BiblicalUsage: Lydia was a seller of purple from Thyatira who worshipped God, and when Paul preached at Philippi, the Lord opened her heart to attend to the things he spoke. She was baptised with her household and pressed Paul and his companions to stay in her house, and after their release from prison they went again to her house to encourage the brethren.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Lydia shows that God opens hearts before anyone preaches a word, and the first convert in Europe was a businesswoman whose home became the church.
